title: Trump Announces Permanent Deal with Denmark for Security in Greenland
seoTitle: Trump Announces Permanent Greenland Security Deal with.
subtitle: The US president signed a pact preventing adversary military bases on the Arctic island
excerpt: Donald Trump announced an agreement with Denmark securing permanent US control over Greenland's defense, preventing rival military presence.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Friday, October 18, United States President Donald Trump disclosed an agreement with Denmark that grants the US permanent control over Greenland's security and defense. The announcement drove online searches and brought the topic to the forefront of the news.

What the US-Denmark Agreement Establishes

According to Trump's post on Truth Social, the treaty prevents American adversaries from maintaining military bases or making sensitive investments on the island without US authorization. The document, scheduled to be signed next week, stipulates that no country may establish a military presence in Greenland without American approval.

Strategic Motivations of the United States

The US considers Greenland strategic for national security, particularly in light of melting Arctic ice, which could open new shipping routes. The region also hosts potential defense routes capable of intercepting missiles coming from Europe or the Arctic.

Reaction from Denmark and Greenland

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated that the treaty strengthens common security in the Arctic and North Atlantic, benefiting NATO and Europe. Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen declared that the agreement recognizes the island's interests and its self-determination.

Context of Tension and History of American Interest

The pact comes after months of bilateral tension, during which Trump threatened the European Union with tariffs and described Greenland as "a piece of ice." In the past, the president had already advocated for the US annexation of the island and maintained a military base in the region.

Implications for Arctic Geopolitics

The agreement arrives at a time when China is demonstrating interest in Arctic routes, investing in icebreaker ships and seeking strategic minerals. By securing permanent control, the US aims to limit the presence of potential rivals in the region while affirming support for Danish sovereignty and the self-determination of the Greenlandic people.

With information from G1.
